title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 6 (Administrative assistance)

content.overview: Section 6 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 permits the parties, or the arbitral tribunal with the parties' consent, to arrange administrative assistance by a suitable institution or person in order to facilitate the conduct of arbitral proceedings.
content.glance: Parties or the tribunal (with consent) may arrange administrative assistance to facilitate proceedings.
content.study: Section 6 is a procedural-support provision. Parties may arrange administrative assistance by a suitable institution or person. The tribunal may do so only with the parties' consent. Assistance is administrative only and does not transfer adjudicatory power.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Facilitates conduct of arbitral proceedings through administrative assistance; not a source of adjudicatory jurisdiction.

sections.heading: Party-arranged assistance
sections.body: The parties may arrange administrative assistance by a suitable institution or person.

sections.heading: Tribunal-arranged assistance
sections.body: The tribunal may arrange such assistance only with the consent of the parties.

sections.heading: Nature of assistance
sections.body: Assistance is administrative; it does not transfer the tribunal's adjudicatory mandate.

examples.title: Party-arranged assistance
examples.body: Parties agree to use an arbitral institution for administrative support. Section 6 permits that.

examples.title: Tribunal without consent
examples.body: Tribunal unilaterally appoints an institution for administrative assistance without party consent. Section 6 does not authorise that.

hypotheticals.question: Can the tribunal arrange administrative assistance without party consent?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 6 requires consent of the parties when the tribunal arranges assistance.

rows.left: No extra tribunal-consent condition in s. 6

misconceptions.trap: Tribunal can arrange assistance without party consent.
misconceptions.correction: Section 6 requires party consent for tribunal-arranged assistance.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 6 permit?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Parties, or the tribunal with the parties' consent, may arrange administrative assistance by a suitable institution or person to facilitate arbitral proceedings.

examTips: Do not equate administrative assistance with adjudicatory power.
revisionPoints: Party or tribunal (with consent) may arrange administrative assistance
Administrative only — no transfer of adjudication

tenMark.point: Identify who may arrange administrative assistance
tenMark.application: Parties, or the tribunal with the parties' consent, may arrange assistance.

tenMark.point: State the need for party consent when the tribunal arranges assistance
tenMark.application: Tribunal-initiated assistance requires the parties' agreement under s. 6.

tenMark.point: Distinguish administrative assistance from decision-making on the merits
tenMark.application: Assistance is logistical/secretarial; it does not transfer adjudicatory power.

tenMark.point: Note institutional vs ad hoc settings
tenMark.application: Section 6 supports both; institutional rules may elaborate the mechanism.

sixteenMark.point: Separate administrative tasks from arbitral functions under ss. 18–27
sixteenMark.application: Keep fact-finding and award-making with the tribunal.
